extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations, especially those working in health care and education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for practicing public relations in health care and educational institutions, covering media relations, employee communication, integrated messaging, issues management, measurement, and use of social media and technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trusted clinicians as advocates and spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage highly trusted physicians and other health care professionals as advocates and spokespeople to build positive perceptions and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate strong relationships with physician partners to act as spokespersons on important messages; physicians ranked highest (73%) in trust for health reform guidance in a Gallup Poll, making them especially valuable compared to other industry figures. (See Chapter 13 for opinion leader definition.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand health care business, financing, and policy context
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations practitioners must understand the complex business and financing of health care and how political, regulatory, economic, and technological forces affect the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of national, regional, and local politics, regulations, economic conditions (e.g., recessions), technological innovations (e.g., EHRs), and financial incentives that affect stakeholder cooperation and the organization's ability to deliver care and communicate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee communication as a core PR function
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employee communication as a critical public relations responsibility because engaged employees influence operational performance, patient outcomes, and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a well-planned, well-executed employee communication strategy to promote engagement and align internal messages with external brand messaging; recognize employees as a powerful communication 'voice' and potential champions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt internal communication channels to frontline workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use communication channels that reach frontline health care workers who lack regular intranet or desk access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ written newsletters, bulletin boards, break-room flyers, in-person meetings, computer kiosks in public areas, websites outside the firewall, blogs, podcasts, and smartphones to reach non-desk staff; supervisors and face-to-face contact remain important channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee social media and media-contact policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and enforce policies that discourage unsanctioned media interaction and set expectations for employee social media use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate that posting about the organization on social media carries the same responsibilities as speaking to traditional media; some organizations post social media policies online and require employees to contact PR when approached by media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated communication across PR, internal comms, and marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate public relations, internal communication, and marketing to optimize strengths and present unified, non-fragmented messages to stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work as an integrated team to customize communications to patients, employees, physicians, policy makers, and business audiences; allow nuanced differences in language/style/format but keep the organization's overall voice and strategic messages consistent to avoid consumer confusion and distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic focus—prioritize messages aligned with business goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Be disciplined in message selection: focus on strategic stories that align with organizational priorities rather than attempting to tell every story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify priority areas (e.g., care delivery, corporate citizenship, technological innovation, health reform) and concentrate resources there; coordinate with organizational strategy and business priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure communication effectiveness by message penetration and behavioral impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate communications not merely by media mentions but by whether key brand messages appear in coverage and whether communications influence target publics tied to organizational goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure measurement assesses reflection of key messages (quality, patient centeredness, convenience, preventive care, innovation) and the desired impact on target audiences; refer to evaluation levels (see Chapter 14) for detailed approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain robust online information repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide up-to-date, comprehensive web resources (member/provider/patient portals, news repositories, press releases) because people increasingly use the Internet for health information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that while many use social media for health info, provider websites remain a preferred source of dependable information; maintain an accessible and current site with news and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active, informed leadership on social media strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations professionals should advise and lead organizational decisions about social media use and be active on these platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand how patient portals, EHR platforms, blogs, video chat, and tweets may change patient-provider relationships and use that insight to guide leadership on social media strategy and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid, transparent, credible media relations (especially in crisis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key attributes of effective media relations: transparency, rapid access to decision makers and content experts, clear and credible messaging, and quick response to inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an authorized spokesperson on call 24/7, prepare leaders for interviews, coordinate responses with senior leaders, and ensure PR staff work effectively with leadership to preserve reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to patient complaints under HIPAA constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When patients publicize complaints, respond within HIPAA limits: express concern, commit to investigate, and provide general information without disclosing protected health information unless consent is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policies and procedures, request signed HIPAA releases for specific disclosures, and, if consent is provided, offer factual responses; coordinate communications with legal and subject-matter experts before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media and social media monitoring and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously monitor traditional and online media and classify coverage to inform messaging and crisis response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use media monitoring services or agencies to track coverage and classify it as positive, neutral, or negative; analyze tone, quantity, and frequency to refine future messaging and provide insights to senior leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues management and proactive mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, prevent, and mitigate issues before they become crises through proactive relationship building and risk identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strong relationships with operational leaders and content experts; meet regularly to spot risks, develop mitigation strategies, and activate networks quickly when issues arise; ensure internal communicators and marketers receive key messages promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations as strategic leadership function
rubrics_metrics.description: PR should have a voice at the leadership table, providing stakeholder insights and strategic counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve as thought partners to management, combining internal and external perspectives to inform decisions that serve both stakeholders and organizational interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of PR with resource development and fundraising
rubrics_metrics.description: Align public relations with development/advancement functions to support fundraising and donor engagement, especially in resource-constrained education environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with 501(c)(3) entities and development offices to craft strategies and tactics that raise awareness, cultivate donors, and support institution missions; integrate PR into resource development planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals of public relations in public education
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary PR goals in education: increase awareness of education issues; cultivate stakeholder relationships; gain acceptance/support for initiatives; enhance institutional reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue these objectives to secure funding, community support for reorganizations or curriculum changes, and to influence parents' and students' school choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of social media and technology in education PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ social media tools (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube), websites, and email marketing to push targeted messages and engage stakeholders efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize social media's broad adoption by districts and its impact on journalism; be timely, relevant, thoughtful, and careful in responses; early adopters (e.g., San Diego Unified) demonstrate these tools' utility for K-12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement with web and social analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use analytics to measure reach and engagement: website analytics (unique visitors, pages, duration) and social media metrics (fans, friends, interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools like Google Analytics and platform metrics help evaluate whether content conveys key messages and engages intended publics; use these data to refine content and targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve face-to-face communication and personal accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite digital tools, maintain in-person engagement (town halls, open houses, meetings) because many stakeholders prefer or require face-to-face contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that teachers and frontline staff may not access digital channels frequently; prioritize supervisor communication, conferences, and forums to convey honesty, accessibility, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt PR strategies to funding constraints and rising expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate creatively under shrinking budgets while meeting higher stakeholder expectations for responsiveness and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage low-cost digital tools where appropriate, prioritize messages, integrate with fundraising, and find resourceful ways to engage diverse stakeholder groups including parents, elected officials, and labor unions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and plan for education-specific crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize common crisis types in education (church/state separation issues, hate speech vs. free expression, campus violence, union disputes, governing-board decisions, social-issue controversies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop crisis plans tailored to these scenarios; engage stakeholders early, communicate clearly about policies and actions, and coordinate legal, administrative, and PR responses.
